newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ruling party to discuss Salinas expulsion.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ruling party to discuss Salinas expulsion.

text.p: Mexico's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) will discuss the possible expulsion of disgraced former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari at its National Assembly later this week, party chief Santiago Onate said on Tuesday.

"The party will have to take a position on this matter," Onate told reporters. "It is without doubt a difficult topic, doubtless a delicate topic, on which the Assembly will have opinions and discussions."
He said whatever decision the party takes will have to be based on "statutes, based on the elements we have, and not to satisfy interests which are not necessarily those of the party."
The PRI, which has governed Mexico without interruption since 1929, holds its 17th National Assembly on September 20-22 in Mexico City.
The party expelled the former president's brother Raul Salinas in December last year following his arrest on murder charges and subsequent involvement in an embezzlement scandal.
Its Honour and Justice Commission agreed at the same time to look further into a possible expulsion of the former Mexican president but has yet to take a decision.

Carlos Salinas, whom many Mexicans blame for the December 1994 peso crisis and ensuing deep recession, left Mexico in disgrace following his brother's arrest and is now believed to be living in Ireland.
